elements.element: The licence extends to Client's affiliates without a written-notice condition.
elements.evidence: The grant covers Client's affiliates only “upon written notice to TrueLink,” so affiliate coverage is conditional rather than automatic.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Client's behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants rights only to Client and Client's affiliates; it does not cover contractors.
The clause does not establish that paid-up licences are absent and provides that the licence lasts only until termination of the Agreement.
The clause does not establish that paid-up licences are absent and contains no irrevocability protection.

elements.element: Any subscription licence is terminable only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The clause does not establish that subscription licences are absent and instead permits the licence to end whenever the Agreement is terminated under Section 12, without stating the required uncured-material-breach limitation.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Client's successors.
elements.evidence: Transfer without approval is permitted only to a successor in a merger or acquisition, not to successors generally.

elements.element: Client's affiliates are covered by the licence upon written notice.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly extends the licence to “Client's affiliates upon written notice to TrueLink.”

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 15 permits Client to transfer the licence without approval “to a successor in a merger or acquisition.”

result.reason: The redline implements both fallback requirements and makes no unrelated substantive change. It does not satisfy the preferred position because affiliate coverage requires notice, contractors are omitted, paid-up and subscription protections are absent, and successor transferability is limited to merger or acquisition transactions. Drafting quality is reduced by the unresolved pre-existing fragment ending “so long as such” and some ambiguity around the affiliate grant's singular possessive phrasing.
